a.description: The **Anchor** element creates a hyperlink to web pages, files, email addresses, locations, or anything else a URL can address.

abbr.description: The **Abbreviation** element represents an abbreviation or acronym. The optional `title` attribute provides the full description.

address.description: The **Address** element indicates contact information for a person, group, or organization.

article.description: The **Article** element represents a self-contained composition in a document, page, or site, intended to be independently distributable or reusable.

aside.description: The **Aside** element represents content indirectly related to the main content, like sidebars or call-out boxes.

audio.description: The **Audio** element embeds sound content in documents. It may contain one or more `<source>` elements.

b.description: The **Bring Attention To** element draws attention to text without conveying extra importance. Use `<strong>` for importance.

blockquote.description: The **Block Quotation** element indicates that the enclosed text is an extended quotation. Use the `cite` attribute for the source URL.

body.description: The **Body** element represents the content of an HTML document. There can be only one `<body>` per document.

br.description: The **Line Break** element produces a line break in text. Useful for poems or addresses. **Void element** — no closing tag.

button.description: The **Button** element represents a clickable button. Use `type="submit"`, `type="reset"`, or `type="button"`.

canvas.description: The **Canvas** element provides a resolution-dependent bitmap area for rendering graphics via JavaScript (2D/WebGL).

caption.description: The **Table Caption** element specifies the caption (title) of a table. Must be the first child of `<table>`.

cite.description: The **Citation** element references the title of a creative work (book, paper, poem, film, etc.).

code.description: The **Code** element displays its contents styled as a fragment of computer code. Use with `<pre>` for multi-line code blocks.

col.description: The **Table Column** element defines a column within a table. **Void element** — used within `<colgroup>`.

colgroup.description: The **Table Column Group** element defines a group of columns within a table.

data.description: The **Data** element links content with a machine-readable translation via the `value` attribute.

datalist.description: The **Data List** element contains `<option>` elements representing recommended values for an `<input>` with `list` attribute.

dd.description: The **Description Details** element provides the description or value of a term (`<dt>`) in a description list (`<dl>`).

del.description: The **Deleted Text** element represents text that has been deleted from a document. Use `<ins>` for inserted text.

details.description: The **Details** disclosure widget creates an expandable/collapsible section. `<summary>` provides the visible heading.

dfn.description: The **Definition** element indicates the defining instance of a term within its nearest ancestor content.

dialog.description: The **Dialog** element represents a dialog box or subwindow. Use `.showModal()` for modal behavior.

div.description: The **Content Division** element is a generic block container. Use when no other semantic element is appropriate.

dl.description: The **Description List** element represents a list of term-description groups (`<dt>`/`<dd>` pairs).

dt.description: The **Description Term** element specifies a term in a description list (`<dl>`).

em.description: The **Emphasis** element marks text with stress emphasis. Typically rendered in italic. Nest for stronger emphasis.

embed.description: The **Embed** element embeds external content at the specified point. **Void element** — no closing tag.

fieldset.description: The **Field Set** element groups related form controls and labels. Use `<legend>` to provide a caption.

figcaption.description: The **Figure Caption** element provides a caption or legend for its parent `<figure>` element.

figure.description: The **Figure** element represents self-contained content (images, diagrams, code), optionally with a `<figcaption>`.

footer.description: The **Footer** element represents a footer for its nearest sectioning content. Typically contains author, copyright, or nav links.

form.description: The **Form** element represents a document section containing interactive controls for submitting information. Use `action` and `method` attributes.

h1.description: **Heading level 1** — the highest section level heading. Use only one `<h1>` per page for accessibility.

h2.description: **Heading level 2** — second-level section heading. Organize content hierarchically: h1 > h2 > h3.

h3.description: **Heading level 3** — third-level section heading for subsections within an h2.

h6.description: **Heading level 6** — the lowest section heading level.

head.description: The **Head** element contains machine-readable metadata about the document: title, scripts, stylesheets, meta tags.

header.description: The **Header** element represents introductory content or navigation for its nearest sectioning element.

hr.description: The **Horizontal Rule** element represents a thematic break between paragraph-level elements. **Void element**.

html.description: The **HTML** root element represents the top-level of an HTML document. All other elements must be descendants.

i.description: The **Idiomatic Text** element represents text set apart for idiomatic, technical, or taxonomic reasons (not just italic).

iframe.description: The **Inline Frame** element embeds another HTML page into the current document. Use `sandbox` for security.

img.description: The **Image** element embeds an image. Always include `alt` for accessibility. **Void element** — no closing tag.

input.description: The **Input** element creates interactive form controls. Supports many `type` values: text, password, email, number, checkbox, radio, file, etc. **Void element**.

ins.description: The **Inserted Text** element represents text that has been inserted into a document. Use `<del>` for deleted text.

kbd.description: The **Keyboard Input** element represents user input from a keyboard, voice, or other input device.

label.description: The **Label** element provides a caption for a form control. Use `for` attribute to associate with the control's `id`.

legend.description: The **Legend** element represents a caption for its parent `<fieldset>`. Must be the first child.

li.description: The **List Item** element represents an item in a list (`<ul>`, `<ol>`, or `<menu>`).

link.description: The **External Resource Link** element links the document to external resources (CSS, icons, etc.). **Void element** — used in `<head>`.

main.description: The **Main** element represents the dominant content of the `<body>`. Only one per document, and not inside other landmark elements.

map.description: The **Image Map** element defines clickable areas on an image, used with `` elements and the `usemap` attribute on ``.

mark.description: The **Mark** element highlights text for reference or notation purposes (like search results).

meta.description: The **Metadata** element represents metadata that cannot be expressed by other meta-related elements. **Void element**.

meter.description: The **Meter** element represents a scalar measurement within a known range (disk usage, ratings, scores).

nav.description: The **Navigation** element represents a section with navigation links. Use for major navigation blocks, not every link.

noscript.description: The **No Script** element provides fallback content when JavaScript is disabled or not supported.

object.description: The **Object** element represents an external resource (image, nested browsing context, plugin). Use `` or `

ol.description: The **Ordered List** element represents a numbered list. Use `type` for numbering style, `start` for starting number, `reversed` for descending.

optgroup.description: The **Option Group** element groups `<option>` elements within a `<select>`. Use `label` attribute for the group name.

option.description: The **Option** element defines an item in a `<select>`, `<optgroup>`, or `<datalist>`. Use `value` for the submitted value.

output.description: The **Output** element displays the result of a calculation or user action. Use `for` to associate with inputs.

p.description: The **Paragraph** element represents a paragraph of text. Block-level, automatically closes when another block element starts.

picture.description: The **Picture** element provides art-direction and responsive images. Contains `` elements and one fallback ``.

pre.description: The **Preformatted Text** element displays text exactly as written, preserving whitespace and line breaks. Use `<code>` inside for code.

progress.description: The **Progress** element displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task. Use `value` and `max` attributes.

q.description: The **Inline Quotation** element represents a short inline quotation. Browsers automatically add quotation marks.

s.description: The **Strikethrough** element renders text with a strikethrough. Use `<del>` for deleted text, `<s>` for no-longer-relevant text.

samp.description: The **Sample Output** element represents sample output from a computer program.

script.description: The **Script** element embeds executable code (JavaScript) or links to an external script via `src`. Use `defer` or `async` for performance.

section.description: The **Section** element represents a generic standalone section of a document. Use when no more specific semantic element applies.

select.description: The **Select** element provides a dropdown menu of `<option>` elements. Use `multiple` for multi-select, `size` for visible rows.

small.description: The **Small** element represents side-comments and small print (copyright, legal text). Not for making text visually smaller.

source.description: The **Source** element specifies media resources for `<picture>`, `<audio>`, or `<video>`. **Void element**.

span.description: The **Span** element is a generic inline container. Use when no other semantic element is appropriate.

strong.description: The **Strong Importance** element indicates that its contents have strong importance, seriousness, or urgency. Typically bold.

style.description: The **Style** element contains CSS styling for the document. Typically placed in `<head>`, but can appear anywhere.

sub.description: The **Subscript** element displays text lowered below the baseline (chemical formulas, math).

summary.description: The **Summary** element provides a heading for a `<details>` element. Click to toggle the details visible/hidden.

sup.description: The **Superscript** element displays text raised above the baseline (exponents, footnotes).

table.description: The **Table** element represents tabular data in rows and columns. Use `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, `<td>` for structure.

tbody.description: The **Table Body** element groups the body rows in a table. Browsers auto-insert `<tbody>` if omitted.

td.description: The **Table Data Cell** element defines a data cell in a table. Use `colspan` and `rowspan` to span columns/rows.

template.description: The **Template** element holds HTML fragments not rendered on page load, instantiated via JavaScript at runtime.

textarea.description: The **Textarea** element represents a multi-line plain-text editing control. Use `rows` and `cols` for size, CSS for better control.

tfoot.description: The **Table Foot** element groups the footer rows in a table. Must appear after `<thead>` and before `<tbody>`.

th.description: The **Table Header Cell** element defines a header cell in a table. Use `scope` attribute for accessibility (`col`/`row`).

thead.description: The **Table Head** element groups the header rows in a table. Appears at the top of `<table>`.

time.description: The **Time** element represents a specific period in time. Use `datetime` attribute for machine-readable format.

title.description: The **Title** element defines the document's title shown in the browser tab. **Required** in every HTML document.

tr.description: The **Table Row** element defines a row of cells in a table. Contains `<th>` and `<td>` elements.

u.description: The **Unarticulated Annotation** element represents text with a non-textual annotation (like misspelled words, Chinese proper names).

ul.description: The **Unordered List** element represents a bulleted list of items. Use CSS `list-style-type` to change bullet style.

var.description: The **Variable** element represents a variable in a mathematical expression or programming context. Typically italic.

video.description: The **Video** element embeds a media player for video playback. Use `<source>` for multiple formats. Add `controls` for UI.

wbr.description: The **Word Break Opportunity** element specifies where a line break would be acceptable. **Void element**.

class.description: **Global attribute.** A space-separated list of CSS class names for the element. Use for styling (CSS) and selection (JS).

id.description: **Global attribute.** A unique identifier for the element. Must be unique across the entire document. Used for CSS, JS, and anchors.

style.description: **Global attribute.** Inline CSS styles applied to the element. Prefer external stylesheets for maintainability.

title.description: **Global attribute.** Tooltip text shown on mouse hover. Also important for accessibility with `<iframe>` and `<abbr>`.

href.description: The URL the hyperlink points to. Used with `<a>`, `<link>`, `<area>`, `<base>`. Can be absolute, relative, or fragment (`#id`).

src.description: The URL of the embeddable content. Used with ``, `

alt.description: **Required on ``.** Alternative text when the image cannot be displayed. Critical for accessibility and SEO.

type.description: Defines the type of the element. For `<input>`: text, password, email, number, checkbox, radio, file, submit, etc. For `<button>`: submit, reset, button. For `<script>`: MIME type or `module`.

name.description: The name of the form control. Submitted as the key in form data. Also used for radio button grouping and `<meta>`, `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<param>`.

value.description: The initial value of a form control. For `<input>`: default value. For `<button>`, `<option>`, `<param>`: the submitted value.

placeholder.description: Hint text shown in an empty `<input>` or `<textarea>`. Disappears on focus. Not a substitute for `<label>`.

required.description: **Boolean attribute.** Indicates the form control must have a value before submission. Use with `<input>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>`.

disabled.description: **Boolean attribute.** Makes the form control non-interactive and non-submittable. Use with `<input>`, `<button>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>`, `<fieldset>`, `<optgroup>`, `<option>`.

checked.description: **Boolean attribute.** Pre-selects a checkbox or radio button on page load. Only for `<input type="checkbox">` and `<input type="radio">`.

selected.description: **Boolean attribute.** Pre-selects an `<option>` on page load. If unset, the first `<option>` is selected by default.

readonly.description: **Boolean attribute.** Makes the form control read-only (value can be selected but not changed). Unlike `disabled`, the value is still submitted.

target.description: Where to open the linked URL. `_self` (default), `_blank` (new tab), `_parent`, `_top`, or a frame name. Use `rel="noopener"` with `_blank` for security.

rel.description: The relationship of the linked URL. Common values: `stylesheet`, `icon`, `noopener`, `noreferrer`, `nofollow`, `preload`, `prefetch`, `alternate`, `canonical`.

data-*.description: **Global attribute.** Custom data attributes for storing extra information. Access via `element.dataset` in JavaScript. The `*` can be any valid name.

aria-*.description: **WAI-ARIA attribute.** Accessibility attributes for assistive technologies. Common: `aria-label`, `aria-hidden`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-describedby`, `role`.

action.description: The URL that processes the form submission. Can be relative or absolute. Defaults to the current page if omitted.

method.description: The HTTP method for form submission. `GET` (appends to URL) or `POST` (in request body). Use `POST` for sensitive or large data.

for.description: Associates a `<label>` with a form control by matching the control's `id`. Also used with `<output>` to list associated element IDs.

lang.description: **Global attribute.** The language of the element's content (e.g., `en`, `ko`, `fr`). Important for accessibility and SEO.

tabindex.description: **Global attribute.** Controls tab order. `0` = normal order, `-1` = not reachable by tab (but focusable via JS), positive = custom order (avoid).

hidden.description: **Global boolean attribute.** Hides the element from display. Unlike `display:none`, this is a semantic signal. Don't use for critical content.

content.description: The value for `<meta>` elements. For `name="description"`: page summary. For `name="viewport"`: `width=device-width, initial-scale=1`.

charset.description: Character encoding for the document. Almost always `UTF-8`. Used on `<meta charset="UTF-8">` and `<script charset="...">`.

defer.description: **Boolean attribute.** On `<script>`, downloads the script in parallel and executes after the document is parsed. Use instead of placing scripts at end of body.

async.description: **Boolean attribute.** On `<script>`, downloads the script in parallel and executes as soon as available. Don't use with `defer`.

srcset.description: On `` and ``, provides a set of image URLs for different resolutions/sizes. Browser picks the best match. Format: `url 1x, url2x 2x` or `url 600w, url2 1200w`.

sizes.description: On ``, ``, ``, specifies the intended display size or media condition. Used with `srcset` for responsive images.

loading.description: On `` and `

autocomplete.description: On form controls, enables or disables browser autofill. `on` or `off`, or specific tokens like `email`, `tel`, `new-password`, `street-address`.

multiple.description: **Boolean attribute.** On `<input type="file">` and `<input type="email">`, allows multiple values. On `<select>`, allows multi-select.

maxlength.description: The maximum number of characters allowed in `<input>` or `<textarea>`. Client-side only — always validate server-side.

minlength.description: The minimum number of characters required in `<input>` or `<textarea>`. Client-side validation only.

min.description: The minimum allowed value for numeric `<input>` types (number, range, date, etc.). Used with `max` for range validation.

max.description: The maximum allowed value for numeric `<input>` types. Also used on `<progress>` and `<meter>` to set the upper bound.

step.description: The increment step for numeric `<input>` types. Default: 1. Use `step="any"` for any value. Affects validation arrows.

pattern.description: A JavaScript regular expression the `<input>` value must match. Use `title` to describe the pattern to users.

accept.description: On `<input type="file">`, restricts accepted file types. Values: file extensions (`.jpg,.png`), MIME types (`image/*`), or `audio/*`, `video/*`.

cols.description: The visible width (in average character widths) of a `<textarea>`. Use CSS `width` instead for better control.

rows.description: The visible number of text lines in a `<textarea>`. Use CSS `height` instead for better control.

controls.description: **Boolean attribute.** On `<video>` and `<audio>`, displays browser's built-in playback controls (play, pause, volume, etc.).

autoplay.description: **Boolean attribute.** On `<video>` and `<audio>`, automatically starts playback. Browsers often block unmuted autoplay. Use `muted` together.

loop.description: **Boolean attribute.** On `<video>` and `<audio>`, automatically loops playback. Use sparingly for user experience.

muted.description: **Boolean attribute.** On `<video>` and `<audio>`, mutes the audio by default. Often needed for `autoplay` to work.

poster.description: On `<video>`, a URL for an image shown while the video is downloading or before playback starts.

cite.description: On `<blockquote>`, `<del>`, `<ins>`, `<q>`, specifies a URL pointing to the source of the quote or change.

datetime.description: On `<time>`, a machine-readable date/time. On `<del>` and `<ins>`, the date/time the change was made. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD` or ISO 8601.

colspan.description: On `<td>` and `<th>`, the number of columns the cell should span. Value must be a positive integer.

rowspan.description: On `<td>` and `<th>`, the number of rows the cell should span. Value must be a positive integer.

scope.description: On `<th>`, specifies which cells the header relates to. `col` = column, `row` = row, `colgroup`, `rowgroup`. Important for accessibility.

download.description: On `<a>`, prompts the browser to download the linked resource instead of navigating. Optionally specify a filename.

media.description: On `<source>`, `<link>`, `<style>`, `<a>`, a media query specifying which media the resource applies to (e.g., `screen and (max-width: 600px)`).

sandbox.description: On `<iframe>`, applies security restrictions. Values: `allow-scripts`, `allow-same-origin`, `allow-forms`, `allow-popups`. Empty = maximum restriction.

enctype.description: On `<form>`, the MIME type of the form data. `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (default), `multipart/form-data` (for file uploads), `text/plain`.

novalidate.description: **Boolean attribute.** On `<form>`, disables browser's built-in form validation. Use when providing custom validation.

role.description: **ARIA attribute.** Defines the purpose of an element for assistive technology (e.g., `navigation`, `banner`, `button`, `alert`, `dialog`).
